preamble: Sanskrit does not allow the retroflex sibilant [ʂ] at the end of a word. It is replaced by the retroflex stop [ʈ] word-finally and before the locative plural ending -su (and by [ɖ] before voiced bh, dh). Whitney notes that the change is rare because few stems end in ṣ.

examples.note: Whitney's example of word-final ṣ becoming ṭ.
Before -su, stem-final ṣ becomes the retroflex stop (Whitney §226b); before bh it becomes ḍ (dviḍbhís)
